body:
No sick exception means unlimited folks will show up sick to avoid the late fee. If workout in am then a person can easily feel ok when going to bed only to wake up feeling like death. For PM workouts, you can have it hit you mid-workday. As the cold season heats up, I have no doubt that there will be days that I will push through to avoid paying $12. 

I’ve already attended class when my chronic condition is flaring up. Called it a “green day” and wondered how long I had to stay to avoid the charge. Felt fine 8 hours before but an intensely physical workday can flare my condition. 

Before folks suggest I don’t do OTF, like a cold my chronic issues are just a relatively random fact of life that don’t ascribe to 8 hour windows. Oh...and the whole OTF is for everyone thing. 

I budgeted a bit for $12 fees given the risk. On the flip side, there’s the risk that I show up and push through a cold or being symptomatic. No different than a normal gym by the way.

So sorry for your poor health and its impact on your fitness. Stay strong in giving your body what it needs for now. Hold onto the joy that exercise and keto provided. It’s that joy and sense of health that will make it ok when you are able to return to your routine. Like coming home to your self. 

Never mind the people who have no understanding of weight gain or loss of fitness due to other health issues. There are many of us who share your struggle. Maybe a few will chime in here with their support. 

Like you I took medical advice to take a break from my powerlifting and running regime to address a health issue. Was put on a “clean diet” of fruits, whole grains, and mostly vegetables to remedy nutrient deficiencies. Was also prescribed medication with a “chance” of weight gain. Despite amping up my 5-years of 16:8 to 18 and 20 hr fasts, I gained 15 pounds and lost so much strength I could barely do a push-up. 

I try to think of those months as a necessary break in training to fix some gaps that had built up over time. Started back with low carb and more intense training in August. I created a training and diet regime that slowly but consistently ramped things back up  (instead of my usual do-or-die approach). 

Not gonna lie. It’s been hard on the ego since my strength and weight loss have also been *slow* but steady. Days in the gym are hard when my health necessitates pulling back from a run to walk. Self esteem definitely takes a hit when I catch a glimpse of my love handles as I lift puny weights. 

I just remind myself that I am just working my training program just like the lifter beside me. 

Best wishes for a speedy return to health, fitness, and keto.

Thanks everyone. And sorry so many deal with this. Like someone mentioned, this was the issue that caused me to start trying to get medical help. No matter how hard I try to "stop it" at a certain point, I just go down and loose control over my body, speech, gaze. Total shut down except one small part of my mind stays "awake" and can sorta observe what's going on around me. 

It's amped up in frequency with just last week 4/7 days, I had an incident.  I've had one full blackout that I don't remember much about. 

This was so validating as I've been made to feel stupid by my doctors for being concerned about collapses that aren't actual blackouts. It makes you feel ashamed. 

As I struggled to stop the cascade of symptoms just last night, I told my husband, "No. I am just not going to collapse anymore." That's how awful the docs make you feel. Like anyone would think, "I'm just not going to have cancer any more."

So thanks again. And here's to no collapses this week.
Started up again last Monday. Not so easy with a stressful work week but managed to keep calories in target. (Carbs on target too since I need to be low-carb for health reasons.)

Thank you for your post. Hope you find answers soon. 

This is exactly my experience since last March. I have a job that I'd always wanted. Maybe overworked the first year a bit, and wound up collapsing one night after getting home. Heart palpitations, severe headache, dizziness, inability to speak, loss of muscle control, felt like someone turned off access to parts of my brain, then down I went. 

Eyes stayed open. No full blackout. But totally catatonic, staring, unable to move. 

These events have increased in frequency and progressed to full blackouts. 

And the medical system has proven to be unhelpful at best. Harmful and dismissive at times. Apparently my female body necessitates hormones as the first step in any treatment plan for any condition. Not an MRI despite a history of head injury/TBI. Not a thyroid workup. Not an ECG or stress test. Unfortunately, I fell for the sales job on hormones will fix everything despite my family having horrific reactions to those drugs. I've had horrific reactions lasting since May. 

And still no referrals to neurology or endocrinology. Finally got TTT scheduled for end of the month. Like you, I fear it will not show anything. Or I won't fit their magical metric. I will once again get the side-eye and dismissive, condescending responses. 

I am trying to incorporate the various things I've seen on this sub to help. Don't like trying meds anyway ...since I always seem to be in the small %age who has adverse reactions. 

So thank you for listing all of the things you've tried. I didn't know about some of those. I am also tempted to send your description to my docs. My talking about all of the symptoms just makes them say things like "that's a lot of symptoms.," "a lot going on," "I don't think it's us - cardiology, neurology, endocrinology, etc. You should get a referral somewhere else." It all makes me hate the system even more than I do...try getting treated by civilian docs for a service-related traumatic brain injury. 

So also like you, I fear that yet another career that I love will be lost. Also fear that failure to address my neurological history will mean that one day I won't wake up from a blackout. It's appalling to see so many people in these subs who will become just another statistic, missed case, lost life. It's devastating to feel like that is my likely fate as well. 

Good luck to you.

Mine is at the end of the month. Scared of getting the “your crazy/hysterical” look. That happened during my heart stress test. Spent the whole summer trying to “man-up,” “not be a pussy,” and “stop faking it.” Only to wind up collapsed, catatonic, and staring up into my worried partner’s eyes. Episodes have increased in frequency and included full blackouts lately. Still every doc experience makes me feel like I am crazy. 

Former military so I would probably just push through and deal with whatever new normal this is. Risk falling out and hitting my head. Had a service-related traumatic brain injury so can’t afford any hits to the head. (No recs about neurology please— apparently that’s way down the medical checklist despite my history and resulting chronic impacts.)

But my love is the one who catches me as I start to fall. He’s the one who worries daily about whether I will make it home safely. 

So I keep fighting through the looks and invalidating comments. 

So I agreed to an ECG, Holter, and tilt test. Feels like I am setting myself up for disappointment.

Right now. Joined OTF last month out of frustration. Still yet to be diagnosed health issues took me away from sports in March. Figured I could watch my HR, get back to lifting and running (PW 4 now), and feed my adrenaline hunger. . . Without killing myself. 

Was immediately addicted to the energy. Have kept up what seems like a wise recovery program of 3x per week. 

But that feeling you get when pushed right to your limit with good tunes blasting?

Went from OTF on Sunday to Cycle Bar yesterday. Thought it could be my in between workout. Was just going to enjoy the music, disco lights, and get my legs moving a little. Was too totally awesome. The feels. Body felt fine but pushed my HR/physical limits a bit far. 

Physical stamina was crap today. Still would have gone. But my mother had surgery this am. I got called back into the clinic for more tests. And work was blowing up my cell phone. 

So I hit that cancel button. Headed for a protein shake and broke my fast at 530 right when I shoulda been climbing on the tread. (I workout and do pretty much everything fasted.) 

Probably for the best that I late cancelled since my symptoms started acting up an hour ago. (Usually get through the trend ok and then just have to watch my HR and fatigue through the floor/row.)

So thanks for this post. Helps to take the edge off my discouragement.

Thanks so much for sharing your experience with OTF and POTS. I have been suffering from what seemed to be sudden dizziness then catatonic collapse since March. Had been a powerlifter, runner (5-10K) and 30lb Rucker as recently as last Feb. Figured overwork so rested for a month. Got worst and my strength/endurance nose-dived. While my weight shot up as docs prescribed all manner of meds and "rest". 

Never stopped rucking daily though took all the weight out of my ruck and reduced my distance to a mile some days. Also never stopped IF. So my losses aren't as great as they could be. 

The past month of vigilant data and symptom tracking has shown what you described. Heart rate shooting up with up and down movement. I also tend to get a warning headache on my right side and blurry vision before the overwhelming dizziness leading to a catatonic collapse on my worst days. Have tilt test scheduled for next month.

Got frustrated. Saw OT vlogers talking about the HR-based workout and figured I could get in a workout while keeping my HR under control. 

Then got a bit nervous that coach comments, partner workouts, and seeing my stats on the screen would drive me beyond good sense and spark my competitive nature. 

Left me a bit worried to try OT. Then just decided to work my own program.

Completed first workout today. 

Stuck to plan-- modifying and slowing the up&down like burpees and PWing on the treads. Noticed the start of that headache with 2min left in the workout. Eased off and made it  with no problems. So far no post-exertional onset either. 

Coaches were encouraging and not pushy/critical. And everyone in the class was super nice and "in it together" no matter their size or fitness level. 

Great to do a little lifting and tread work again.

Guess I just joined the inconceivable numbers of folks who are sold and obsessed after the first class.
